character_facts: The future Supreme Metabaron is persistent enough to conduct a vast interplanetary search for knowledge about love.
Steelhead has metal or steel fingers and appears physically destructive when frustrated.
The Central Brain functions as an advising intelligence, directing the seeker to Terra Prima.
Lothar is associated with a hard, anti-romantic philosophy in the exchange on this page.
characters_present: A machine interlocutor identified in dialogue as Lothar
continuity_links: This page continues an ongoing quest by the future Supreme Metabaron to understand or acquire the capacity for love.
The visit to Terra Prima follows a failed wider search across many worlds and satellites.
The destruction of the library material marks another failure in that search.
dialogue_meaning: One machine voice insists that love is a foolish, volatile human concept and says machines have no teacher for it.
Another speaker rebukes that cynical view and urges Lothar to listen, claiming reality contains more than his limited philosophy allows.
Narration explains the Metabaron's desperate search for written knowledge that might explain how to experience love.
Steelhead's outburst shows frustration when the library yields no usable answer.
lore_facts: The future Supreme Metabaron is actively seeking a way to learn or feel love.
His search has already covered more than 3,500 planets and artificial satellites.
Terra Prima is identified as the cradle of humanity.
An 'omni-library' on Terra Prima still exists in immense storage facilities.
Ancient paper on Terra Prima is so fragile that it disintegrates on contact with Steelhead's fingers.
Steelhead can physically destroy enormous quantities of books almost instantly.
plot_events: A machine character dismisses love as something machines cannot understand or learn.
Another voice argues back, saying the machine is being misled by romantic ideas but should listen.
Narration states that the future Supreme Metabaron searches thousands of planets and artificial satellites for a document that could teach him how to feel love.
He is directed by the Central Brain to visit the remains of Terra Prima, described as humanity's cradle, where the omni-library still survives in vast repositories.
Inside the preserved storehouses, ancient paper crumbles at the slightest touch from Steelhead's metal fingers.
Frustrated by finding no useful knowledge, he instantly reduces millions of books to dust.
uncertainties: Several dialogue and narration boxes are small and partially difficult to read, so some names and phrasing may be slightly uncertain.
It is not fully clear from the page alone whether Steelhead and the future Supreme Metabaron are separate characters or the same figure being referred to under different names/titles.
visual_summary: A giant robot-like figure argues with a smaller machine intelligence against a pink mechanical background. The page then shifts to narration over outer space and a distant world, followed by a view of ancient domed ruins on Terra Prima. In enormous library-like storehouses, the mechanical seeker handles fragile old paper that disintegrates, then violently pulverizes the remaining books into a white storm of dust.
